## **2\. Product Background** {#2.-product-background}

Electrical infrastructure inspection is important for identifying visible defects in assets such as towers, conductors, insulators, and associated equipment. Conventional inspection may require substantial field effort, while UAV-based image collection can support safer observation and more systematic documentation of asset conditions.

UAV inspection produces images and other evidence that must be organized, reviewed, associated with inspection activities and assets, and followed up when defects are confirmed. When mission records, visual evidence, AI results, and maintenance information are handled separately, tracking the status and history of an inspection becomes more difficult.

Publicly documented initiatives demonstrate the relevance of UAV and AI technology to power-grid inspection in Vietnam. EVN reported recognition of a UAV/AI initiative developed by Quang Tri Power Company, and EVNCPC has published information on UAV-based inspection and AI-related development. These cases are used as background references; they do not establish an enterprise requirement or partnership for this capstone.

UAV-PMS is independently proposed and developed by the student team as an academic capstone project. It is not commissioned, sponsored, or formally validated by EVN, EVNSPC, EVNCPC, or their affiliated units. The team defines and evaluates its own prototype requirements, focusing on inspection mission management, AI-assisted defect detection, emergency alerts, GIS-based visualization, evidence review, and maintenance follow-up.

## **3\. Existing Systems** {#3.-existing-systems}

### **3.1 QTPC UAV AI Distribution Grid Inspection System** {#3.1-qtpc-uav-ai-distribution-grid-inspection-system}

**Description:** Quang Tri Power Company (QTPC) reports a UAV, Internet of Things (IoT), and AI system for inspecting distribution-grid assets and warning of safety risks. Its June 2026 presentation describes an inspection workflow, a flight-control application, a central WebApp, AI services, and interfaces to internal EVN/EVNCPC systems.  
**Actors:** QTPC's workflow shows managers using the Web client, field staff or drone operators using the mobile and flight-control applications, and technical staff reviewing AI results and inspection records.Inferred from the documented workflow.  
**Features:** The documented workflow covers inspection planning and route selection, UAV data capture, image and flight-history storage, AI-assisted detection and warning, technical review of findings, GIS or map views, inspection forms, and API connections to internal systems. The report describes visible-light and thermal inspection modes.  
**Pros:** QTPC's system connects flight planning, UAV inspection, AI-assisted detection, technical review, and inspection records in one operational process. It also provides GIS views, flight history, and asset information for grid inspection. The reported pilot inspected more than 180 km of power lines, demonstrating use in a Vietnamese electricity operation.   
**Cons:** The inspection workflow passes approved results to PMIS/KTHT for subsequent handling, so presentation shows approved results being passed to PMIS/KTHT with other systems rather than being shown as a complete maintenance lifecycle within this system. QTPC also reports that image storage must be upgraded for shared use and a more powerful GPU is needed for wider deployment. 

### **3.2 Optelos Power Utility Inspection Platform**  {#3.2-optelos-power-utility-inspection-platform}

**Description:** Optelos is a platform for managing power-utility inspections, from scheduling and drone data intake to AI analysis and maintenance action.  
**Actors:** Utility inspection managers, drone pilots or contractors, analysts reviewing defects, and teams dispatched to investigate them.  
**Features:** Job scheduling and tracking; drone image and video intake; data quality checks; AI-assisted identification of assets and defects; geolocated findings; reports; and trouble tickets linked to repair dispatch.  
**Pros:** Optelos connects inspection evidence, defect location, prioritization, and follow-up action in one workflow. Its published functions include both scheduling and ticketing, making it a strong reference for those parts of UAV-PMS.  
**Cons:** The workflow depends on uploading data to a central vendor platform and connecting it with a utility’s existing GIS, ticketing, or asset-management systems. Adopting the complete workflow therefore requires data-transfer and integration arrangements.

### **3.3 Hepta Insights Power-Line Inspection Platform** {#3.3-hepta-insights-power-line-inspection-platform}

**Description:** Hepta Insights is an AI-assisted platform focused on inspecting power lines and reviewing the condition of grid assets.  
**Actors:** Grid operators, qualified inspectors, engineering teams, managers, and maintenance crews.  
Features: Aggregation of RGB, infrared, and LiDAR data; asset-based digital models; AI-assisted defect screening; inspector review; cloud access to inspection data; PDF/XLS reports; and integration with customer workflows.  
**Pros:** Hepta is purpose-built for power-grid inspection. It brings together several image and sensor types, links findings to assets, and retains a human review step before inspection results inform decisions.  
**Cons:** Hepta states that its specialized AI models are based on customer asset data and that inspection data is made available through its cloud platform. A utility must therefore provide suitable data and establish the necessary data and system integrations to use these capabilities effectively.

### **3.4 Skydio 3D Scan** {#3.4-skydio-3d-scan}

**Description:** Skydio 3D Scan is software for planning autonomous drone flights and capturing images of physical assets. UAV-PMS uses it as a reference for the flight-planning and image-collection stages, not as a power-line inspection management system.  
**Actors:** Drone operators and inspection or surveying teams responsible for defining the capture area, conducting flights, and reviewing the collected images.  
**Features:** The operator defines an area or asset to capture. The software plans a flight path that adapts to the asset’s geometry, controls image coverage and overlap, supports repeatable capture, and lets the team review coverage before exporting images for further processing.  
**Pros:** Adaptive flight planning and coverage review help teams collect consistent images of complex structures. These functions are useful references when designing how UAV-PMS plans inspection flights and checks whether sufficient visual evidence was captured.  
**Cons:** Skydio 3D Scan focuses on flight execution and data capture. The workflow described for this product does not cover power-grid defect classification, confirmation of findings, or maintenance follow-up. UAV-PMS therefore needs its own processes for those stages after images have been collected.

### **3.5 DJI Matrice 30T and Pilot 2 Powerline Inspection**  {#3.5-dji-matrice-30t-and-pilot-2-powerline-inspection}

**Description:** DJI Enterprise offers drone, camera, flight-planning, and data-management solutions for inspecting transmission and distribution lines.  
**Actors:** Drone pilots, inspection staff, remote-operation staff, and personnel who review inspection images and reports.  
**Features:** DJI describes waypoint-based or scheduled inspection missions, reusable flight routes, visual and thermal image capture, and data management through products such as DJI Pilot 2 and FlightHub 2\. Available functions depend on the selected drone, camera, dock, and software configuration.  
**Pros:** The Matrice 30T and DJI Pilot 2 support waypoint missions that can be saved and repeated for subsequent power-line inspections. The drone captures both visual and thermal images, giving inspectors evidence of visible conditions and abnormal equipment temperatures.  
**Cons:** In the Matrice 30T workflow described by DJI, inspectors analyze the captured photographs manually to identify and locate defects. Inspection data must then be connected to an asset-management system for further analysis and maintenance planning.

## **4\. Business Opportunity** {#4.-business-opportunity}

The project addresses a software engineering opportunity to integrate inspection planning, UAV-collected evidence, AI-assisted defect analysis, and maintenance follow-up in a single prototype workflow. The motivation is based on the team’s study of the inspection domain and existing products, rather than on a formally assigned enterprise project.

The reference systems reviewed above provide examples of flight planning, asset inspection, AI analysis, geospatial visualization, and maintenance coordination. UAV-PMS brings selected capabilities together for an academic demonstration, with a team-developed UAV prototype, centralized server-side AI inference for inspection-image analysis; the UAV itself does not run AI inference.

The expected value of the capstone is a demonstrable and testable end-to-end workflow, not a claim of deployment readiness or measurable business benefits for a specific electricity utility. Its feasibility will be assessed through software testing, model evaluation, controlled demonstrations, and clearly labeled sample or simulated operational data where real enterprise records are unavailable.

## **5\. Software Product Vision** {#5.-software-product-vision}

For inspection managers, UAV operators, and maintenance personnel who need to coordinate inspection activities and review potential infrastructure defects, UAV-PMS is an independently developed prototype platform that connects UAV inspection records, AI-assisted visual analysis, geographic context, and maintenance follow-up.

The system supports mission planning and assignment, asset and evidence management, one server-side AI inference service using the best-performing validated model, human validation of detection results, emergency alert handling, GIS monitoring, and maintenance ticket tracking. It aims to improve traceability across these steps within a controlled capstone environment.

Unlike a standalone object detector or drone flight-control application, UAV-PMS demonstrates how detection outputs can be incorporated into a broader inspection and maintenance workflow. Its functionality and performance will be validated within the available prototype and test conditions, without claiming integration into an operational utility environment.

## **6\. Project Scope & Limitations** {#6.-project-scope-&-limitations}

### **6.1 Major Features** {#6.1-major-features}

• FE-01: Identity & Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) – authenticate users, manage user accounts and personnel qualifications, enforce granular role-based permissions (Administrator, Manager, Inspector/Pilot, Technician, Analyst), and restrict data access by regional geographic scope.  
• FE-02: Mission Planning & Field Management – evaluate resource availability (pilot and UAV), schedule and dispatch inspection missions, validate on-site pilot arrival via GPS field check-in (geofence \<= 200m), track near-real-time flight telemetry (with 15–30s transmission latency), and record mission completion.  
• FE-03: Post-flight Data Ingestion & Cloud AI – ingest inspection media (RGB/Thermal photos) post-flight with automatic EXIF GPS coordinate extraction, trigger server-side deep learning inference across the six defect classes, and store detection bounding boxes, confidence scores, and anomaly alerts.  
• FE-04: Analyst Review & Validation – provide an interactive inspection viewer displaying defect bounding boxes, confidence values, and severity levels for human analysts to confirm, reject, correct findings, request reanalysis, and triage critical anomalies.  
• FE-05: Asset & GIS Monitoring – visualize power lines, towers, and periodic UAV flight telemetry on interactive Leaflet maps, inspect tower maintenance history, and manage verified spatial coordinates.  
• FE-06: Maintenance Ticket Management – automatically or manually generate maintenance tickets from confirmed defect findings, assign technicians, monitor repair status, and verify ticket closure.  
• FE-07: Operational Reporting & Export – provide a centralized dashboard of inspection metrics, filter defect statistics by mission, line, or tower asset, and export formal reports in CSV, Excel, and PDF formats.

### **6.2 Limitations & Exclusions** {#6.2-limitations-&-exclusions}

• LI-1: The UAV is a student-built prototype and is not a certified commercial inspection platform. Field demonstrations are subject to safety, weather, and legal constraints.  
• LI-2: The system does not perform physical maintenance or repairs and does not substitute for certified engineering decisions.  
• LI-3: Airspace clearance, flight permissions, and pilot licensing remain outside the scope of the software platform.  
• LI-4: Flight control, navigation autopilot, and obstacle avoidance are handled by the pilot or onboard flight controller; the system does not support autonomous flight teleoperation.  
• LI-5: No direct integration with EVN/EVNSPC enterprise systems (SCADA, PMIS, KTHT) is included in this academic release.  
• LI-6: The defect taxonomy is strictly limited to the six evaluated classes (insulator, insulator\_broken, insulator\_flashover, bird\_nest, foreign\_object, broken\_strand).  
• LI-7: AI defect detection and anomaly extraction are performed post-flight on the server side upon media upload; real-time in-flight edge AI detection and live video stream inference are excluded.  
• LI-8: UAV telemetry is transmitted periodically subject to field mobile network coverage, with an expected latency of 15–30 seconds; continuous zero-latency flight monitoring is not supported.  
• LI-9: Formal hardware custody transfer (drone handover protocol) is excluded; the assigned pilot directly oversees the UAV during the field session.  
• LI-10: Defect spatial mapping relies on camera EXIF GPS metadata and linked tower coordinates; 3D defect triangulation requires dedicated LiDAR/photogrammetry which is not included.  
• LI-11: Long-term asset health index (AHI) calculations and predictive lifecycle forecasting are excluded.  
• LI-12: The prototype is developed for academic demonstration and evaluation, not for production-grade or nationwide deployment.
